name: Methane Liquefaction Linde Cycle (sparse)
description: Methane gas is compressed and cooled through a series of stages to reach high pressure and cryogenic temperature, then expanded to produce a two-phase mixture. The liquid fraction is recovered as liquid methane product, and the vapour is recycled to the compression inlet.
notes: L0 (sparse) variant of VAL_01. Deliberately omits all operating conditions, stage counts, and structural specifics. Only identifies the process (Linde liquefaction), feedstock (methane), and general operation sequence (compress → cool → expand → separate → recycle vapour). Topology extraction and design inference are both required. Reference: benchmark/reference_flowsheets/VAL_01_reference.json (same as VAL_01 and VALS_01). No tag-pattern physics checks — model is free to choose any unit tags.

name: Hydrodealkylation Toluene to Benzene (sparse)
description: Toluene is reacted with hydrogen at high temperature to produce benzene by hydrodealkylation. The reactor effluent is cooled and the vapour and liquid phases are separated. The hydrogen- and methane-rich vapour is recycled to the reactor feed. The benzene-rich liquid is distilled to recover a high-purity benzene product, and unreacted toluene from the column bottoms is recycled to the reactor.
notes: L0 (sparse) variant of VAL_03. Identifies the process (HDA toluene to benzene), feedstock (toluene + hydrogen), and operation sequence (heat → react → cool → separate → distill → dual recycle) without stating any operating conditions, conversion, pressures, or temperatures. Reference: benchmark/reference_flowsheets/VAL_03_reference.json (same as VAL_03). No tag-pattern physics checks.

name: Hydrogen Production Biogas Reforming WGS PSA (sparse)
description: Biogas containing methane and carbon dioxide is converted to a hydrogen-rich gas stream by steam reforming. The syngas passes through water-gas shift reactors to increase the hydrogen fraction, water is condensed and removed, and the dry gas is purified to yield a high-purity hydrogen product. A tail gas is produced as a by-product.
notes: L0 (sparse) variant of VAL_04. Identifies the process (biogas SMR + WGS + PSA), feedstock (biogas + steam), and sequence (compress → reform → shift × 2 → condense water → PSA → H2 product + tail gas) without stating any temperatures, pressures, or reactor conditions. Compounds list carries only the 5 from the L1 case (omits N2, O2 from the reference combustion section, which the L0 description does not mention). Reference: benchmark/reference_flowsheets/VAL_04_reference.json (same as VAL_04). No tag-pattern physics checks.
